newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore retail space to grow 3.5 pct/yr to 2000.
newsitem.headline: Singapore retail space to grow 3.5 pct/yr to 2000.

text.p: Singapore Minister for Trade and Industry Yeo Cheow Tong said on Sunday the potential supply of retail space in the city-state was expected to grow by an average of 3.5 percent per year between 1996 and 2000.
Yeo said in a speech at the opening of a suburban shopping mall that this increase would bring the total stock of retail space to 3.5 million sq metres by the turn of the century.

He said the government's Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) had tapered off its release of land since 1993 but said it would still take some time to turn around what he described as an "oversupply of retail space in the market".

Many of Singapore's large department stores have faced tight margins or losses over the last few years which they have blamed on relatively high rental and overhead costs and on sluggish retail demand.
Hong Kong's Lane Crawford, France's Galeries Lafayette and Kmart Corp of the United States all closed their stores in Singapore in 1996.
